content: You are a programming expert.

You will be given the root cause of a bug, the commit message and the corresponding patch.
        You need to extract all code statements that lead to the bug from the patch, based on the root cause and the commit message.

        Root cause:
        The bug was caused by the `apparmor_task_kill` function not properly releasing the references to the task credentials (`tc`) and the credential label (`cl`) when handling a passed-in credential. This oversight led to a reference count leak, as the function would return early without decrementing the reference counts, resulting in memory not being freed appropriately.
        
        Commit message:
        apparmor: Fix ref count leak in task_kill

apparmor_task_kill was not putting the task_cred reference tc, or the
cred_label reference tc when dealing with a passed in cred, fix this
by using a single fn exit.

Fixes: 90c436a64a6e ("apparmor: pass cred through to audit info.")
Signed-off-by: John Johansen <john.johansen@canonical.com>  
        
        Patch:
        diff --git a/security/apparmor/lsm.c b/security/apparmor/lsm.c
index 3eb992801a7f..d851a6cc19d3 100644
--- a/security/apparmor/lsm.c
+++ b/security/apparmor/lsm.c
@@ -954,7 +954,6 @@ static int apparmor_task_kill(struct task_struct *target, struct kernel_siginfo
 		cl = aa_get_newest_cred_label(cred);
 		error = aa_may_signal(cred, cl, tc, tl, sig);
 		aa_put_label(cl);
-		return error;
 	} else {
 		cl = __begin_current_label_crit_section();
 		error = aa_may_signal(current_cred(), cl, tc, tl, sig);
